domain_symbols.algebraic_invariant: groups and homology-type invariants attached to spaces

rules.name: Homotopy equivalence seed
rules.input_form: maps f : X -> Y and g : Y -> X
preconditions: The compositions gf and fg are homotopic to the respective identity maps
rules.operation: Recognize spaces as homotopy equivalent through mutually inverse maps up to homotopy.
examples: Contractible spaces are homotopy equivalent to a point
counterexamples: A mere bijection without homotopy data is insufficient

rules.name: Fundamental group seed
preconditions: A basepoint is fixed and loop concatenation is defined
rules.operation: Form the fundamental group from homotopy classes of based loops.
examples: The circle has a nontrivial fundamental group generated by winding number
counterexamples: Paths with different endpoints do not define based loops without closure

rules.name: Simply connected criterion seed
rules.output_form: simply connected iff every loop contracts
preconditions: Path connectivity is established
rules.operation: Classify a space as simply connected by contraction of loops.
examples: Euclidean space of dimension at least 2 is simply connected
counterexamples: The punctured plane is not simply connected

rules.name: Euler characteristic seed
preconditions: A valid finite decomposition is fixed
rules.operation: Compute Euler characteristic as an alternating count of cells or simplices.
examples: A sphere has Euler characteristic 2 in standard cell decompositions
counterexamples: Summing cells without alternating signs is invalid

rules.name: Homology functoriality seed
preconditions: Homology theory is fixed on the source and target spaces
rules.operation: Transfer homology through continuous maps in a composition-compatible way.
examples: Topological maps transfer algebraic invariants functorially across spaces
counterexamples: Arbitrary set maps do not induce homology morphisms in general

rules.name: Covering space lifting seed
rules.input_form: covering map and compatible base path or homotopy
preconditions: The standard initial-point compatibility hypotheses hold
rules.operation: Lift path or homotopy data through a covering map.
examples: Covering maps transfer path data upstairs once the starting point is fixed compatibly
counterexamples: Arbitrary endpoint choices do not in general determine a valid lift

rules.name: van Kampen theorem seed
rules.input_form: space decomposed into path-connected open sets with path-connected overlap
rules.output_form: fundamental group assembled from subgroup data
preconditions: The standard van Kampen hypotheses hold
rules.operation: Compute a fundamental group by gluing generators and relations from an admissible open cover.
examples: Decomposition into overlapping open pieces can reduce a fundamental-group computation to generators and relations
counterexamples: Applying van Kampen without path-connected overlap hypotheses is invalid in the standard form

rules.name: Chain complex boundary-square-zero rule
rules.output_form: partial_(n-1) composed with partial_n equals zero
preconditions: A chain complex grading and boundary maps are fixed
rules.operation: Enforce the chain-complex consistency condition that boundaries of boundaries vanish.
examples: Boundaries of boundaries vanish, enabling homology quotient construction
counterexamples: Allowing arbitrary consecutive boundary maps that do not compose to zero is invalid for a chain complex

rules.name: Mayer-Vietoris seed
rules.output_form: long exact sequence relating union, pieces, and overlap
preconditions: The standard Mayer-Vietoris overlap hypotheses hold
rules.operation: Relate invariants of a union to invariants of overlapping subspaces.
examples: Mayer-Vietoris computes homology or cohomology by gluing information from manageable subspaces
counterexamples: Using disjoint nonoverlapping decompositions in place of the required overlap structure is invalid

rules.name: Cup product seed
preconditions: A cohomology theory with cup-product structure is fixed
rules.operation: Multiply cohomology classes to obtain graded ring information.
examples: Cohomology carries more structure than graded groups once cup products are tracked
counterexamples: Treating cohomology multiplication as degree-blind ordinary commutative multiplication is invalid

rules.name: Singular homology seed
preconditions: The standard singular-chain construction is fixed
rules.operation: Build homology from singular chains and their boundary operators.
examples: Continuous maps on spaces induce chain maps and therefore homology morphisms in singular homology
counterexamples: Assigning arbitrary generators with no simplex or boundary structure is invalid

rules.name: Reduced homology normalization rule
preconditions: The ordinary homology theory is fixed
rules.operation: Normalize degree-zero homology by passing to reduced homology.
examples: Reduced homology removes the isolated base contribution in degree zero for connected spaces
counterexamples: Treating reduced and unreduced homology as identical in all degrees and spaces is invalid

rules.name: Long exact sequence of a pair seed
rules.output_form: long exact sequence relating A, X, and (X,A)
preconditions: The standard pair and relative homology setup is active
rules.operation: Relate relative and absolute invariants through the long exact sequence of a pair.
examples: Exactness links relative and absolute invariants into one computational chain
counterexamples: Replacing exactness by arbitrary adjacent maps is invalid

rules.name: Hurewicz theorem seed
rules.input_form: connected space with standard Hurewicz hypotheses
rules.output_form: controlled map from homotopy to homology
preconditions: The relevant connectivity hypotheses hold
rules.operation: Relate early homotopy groups to homology through the Hurewicz morphism.
examples: First nontrivial homotopy groups may be reflected in corresponding homology groups when connectivity assumptions hold
counterexamples: Using Hurewicz conclusions with no connectivity hypotheses is invalid

rules.name: Characteristic class seed
preconditions: A bundle theory and target cohomology theory are fixed
rules.operation: Assign cohomological invariants to bundles.
examples: Bundle nontriviality can be detected through characteristic-class data rather than only through local trivializations
counterexamples: Treating every bundle as characteristic-class trivial is invalid in general

rules.name: Canonical form normalization expansion
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Rewrite expressions into a canonical form that preserves the active equivalence relation.
examples: x + y and y + x map to a shared canonical additive form in commutative settings
counterexamples: Applying canonicalization rules outside their preconditions is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions

rules.name: Substitution soundness expansion
rules.input_form: expression F(x) with admissible substitution x <- g
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Substitute only under explicit domain and structural admissibility constraints.
examples: Replacing a variable by a constrained expression must preserve declared domain assumptions
counterexamples: Substitution that violates assumptions is invalid

rules.name: Approximation error budget expansion

rules.name: Parameter sensitivity expansion
